title: Surjective dimension-attaining open restriction of a flat morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $d\in\mathbb N$. For $b\in Y$ write $X_b=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ for its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Suppose $\dim_a(X_{f(a)})=d$ for every $a\in X$, where the point of the fibre corresponding to $a$ is understood and $\dim_a$ denotes the minimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. For every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, there exist open subschemes $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq Y$ containing $x$, $y$, respectively, such that $f(U)=V$, $\dim U=\dim_xX$, and $\dim V=\dim_yY$. Here $\dim$ is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The restricted morphism $h:U\to V$, $h(a)=f(a)$, is surjective, flat and locally of finite type; $U$ and $V$ are locally Noetherian. For every $a\in U$, the fibre $U_{h(a)}=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h(a))$ satisfies $\dim_a(U_{h(a)})=d$. No relation between $\dim U$ and $\dim V$ is asserted.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$. By the minimum in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], choose open neighbourhoods $U_0\ni x$ and $V_0\ni y$ with $\dim U_0=\dim_xX$ and $\dim V_0=\dim_yY$. The two collections of neighbourhoods are nonempty (they contain the whole spaces), and the definition includes attainment of the minimum, even when its value is $+\infty$.

The target $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $f$ is locally of finite type, so [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation. Together with the assumed flatness, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] therefore says that the underlying map of $f$ is open. No quasi-compactness or global finite presentation is needed.

source.place: Tags 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation), part (1), and 01UA (lemma-fppf-open), as cited in 0AFE

proof.text: Set $U=U_0\cap f^{-1}(V_0)$, an open neighbourhood of $x$ by continuity, and set $V=f(U)$. Step 2 makes $V$ open; it contains $y$ and is contained in $V_0$. The minimum defining local dimension and [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] give $\dim_xX\leq\dim U\leq\dim U_0=\dim_xX$ and $\dim_yY\leq\dim V\leq\dim V_0=\dim_yY$. Hence both dimensions are attained simultaneously. The restriction $h:U\to V$ is the restriction of the continuous map and its structure-sheaf map, using the open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]; since $f(U)=V$, it is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0AFE (lemma-rel-dimension-dimension), first proof paragraph; Topology Tag 0055 (definition-Krull), following remark

proof.text: Open subschemes carry restricted structure sheaves [def-weil-open-immersion], so for $a\in U$ and $b=h(a)$ their stalks are $\mathcal O_{U,a}=\mathcal O_{X,a}$ and $\mathcal O_{V,b}=\mathcal O_{Y,b}$, with the same induced local homomorphism. This proves flatness of $h$ directly by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Also $U$ and $V$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]: every affine open of the open subscheme $U$ (resp. $V$) is, with the same ring of sections, an affine open of $X$ (resp. $Y$), so its ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]; covering $U$ (resp. $V$) by its affine opens gives the defining affine cover with Noetherian rings. No claim about finite-dimensional local rings is used.

source.place: Tag 0AFE (lemma-rel-dimension-dimension), preservation under shrinking; Tag 01U3 (definition-flat); Tags 01T5 and 01T6 for the open-subscheme remark in pqf-def-locnoeth

proof.text: To check that $h$ is locally of finite type, take any affine opens $A\subseteq U$ and $B\subseteq V$ with $h(A)\subseteq B$. Since $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq Y$ are open subschemes with restricted structure sheaves, these same $A,B$ are affine opens in $X,Y$, with unchanged rings of sections and induced ring map. Applying the forward implication of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to $f$ says that $\mathcal O_Y(B)\to\mathcal O_X(A)$ is of finite type. It is exactly $\mathcal O_V(B)\to\mathcal O_U(A)$. The reverse implication of that same lemma now proves that $h$ is locally of finite type.

proof.text: For $a\in U$ put $b=h(a)=f(a)$. The fibre homeomorphisms in [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identify $|X_b|$ with $f^{-1}(b)$ and $|U_b|$ with $h^{-1}(b)=U\cap f^{-1}(b)$, both with the subspace topology. Thus $|U_b|$ is the open subspace of $|X_b|$ cut out by $U$, and it contains the point corresponding to $a$. These identifications preserve opens and chains of irreducible closed subsets, hence preserve the dimensions and their neighbourhood minima. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] to this open subspace: $\dim_a(U_b)=\dim_a(X_b)=d$, the last equality being the hypothesis on $f$. This proves all clauses; if $X$ is empty there is no $x$ to consider.
